speaker_role: independent counselor/consultancy marketer (Park Hye-sung, Admissions Paradigm)
commercial_incentive: Yes - channel is explicitly a consulting service ('Admissions Paradigm'), invites viewers to comment their situation for personalized feedback
key_insights: Illustrates the submit/don't-submit decision through two contrasting mentee examples: a student who skipped SAT prep entirely to invest time in a strong personal-impact essay and activities (admitted test-optional to a top liberal arts college), versus a student with a middling 3.8 GPA but strong 1530 SAT who submitted scores specifically to offset the weaker GPA (admitted with scholarship)

General rule offered: submit scores if above the university's average, if GPA is comparatively weak and needs supplementing, if applying to math/logic-heavy majors (STEM, business, econ), or to establish English-language credibility as an international applicant
Distinguishes test-optional (scores considered if submitted) from test-blind (scores not considered at all, even if submitted) and cites UC Berkeley/UCLA as test-blind examples
Frames the core decision question as: 'Am I strong enough without scores, or does submitting improve my overall impression?'
specific_numbers_or_facts: Example mentee scored 1530 SAT with a 3.8 GPA and was advised to submit scores

UC Berkeley and UCLA cited as adopting test-blind policies (policy accurate as of the UC system's stance during the test-blind period, though this has since evolved and should be re-verified for currency)
notable_or_distinctive: Clearly distinguishes test-optional from test-blind policies with concrete named examples (UC schools), a distinction many similar videos blur together.
reliability_notes: Short, promotional video built around two anecdotal, unverifiable student examples; UC test-blind status is time-sensitive and policy has shifted in recent cycles, so viewers should verify current policy directly rather than relying on this video's snapshot.
